title: SQL Commands: DELETE
summary: Completes CRUD with DELETE FROM ... WHERE, and warns about omitting the WHERE clause.

concepts.heading: DELETE FROM
points: Syntax: DELETE FROM table_name WHERE condition removes every row that matches the condition.
Example: remove the pencil with DELETE FROM products WHERE name = 'Pencil'. Matching on the unique id is safer and clearer: DELETE FROM products WHERE id = 2. Names can repeat; a primary key cannot.
Without WHERE the statement deletes all rows in the table, so the data is lost. Re-read the statement before running it.
After the delete only the pen row remains. With INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE the full CRUD set has now been covered in SQL.
(Extra) DELETE removes rows only; the table and its columns stay. Removing the table itself is a separate command (DROP TABLE).

code_examples.caption: Delete by id (preferred) and the dangerous form

pitfalls: Running DELETE with no WHERE clause wipes the table's rows.
Filtering on a non-unique column (such as name) can remove more than one record.

gaps_and_ideas: Include in the combined SQL CRUD lesson: delete the pencil by id, then predict the outcome of DELETE without WHERE (do it only on a throwaway table in the demo).
